The braking system of a car includes two cylinders containing an incompressible oil, linked by a flexible tube that also contains oil. There is a freely moving piston in each cylinder. One piston is labelled X, and the other is labelled Y in the diagram.
When the driver presses on the brake pedal, a force is exerted on piston X. The pressure produced in the oil by this force is transmitted through the oil so that it causes a force to act on piston Y. This presses the brakes against the moving parts.
The diameter of piston X is $4.0 \text{ cm}$. The diameter of piston Y is $12.0 \text{ cm}$.
The driver exerts a force of $36.0 \text{ N}$ on piston X and it moves a distance of $5.4 \text{ cm}$ to the right.
What is the resultant force on piston Y and how far does it move along the cylinder?
